card.description:
**Location** Frederick, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264437 **Date posted** 15/11/2026

 

**Director Biochemical & Biophysical Methods**

**Reports to:** Senior Director, Global Technical Operations – Manufacturing Process and Analytical Science – Analytical

**Location:** Frederick, MD USA

Located on the Frederick, MD Manufacturing Campus, GTO operates a state-of-the-art laboratory equipped with modern analytical instrumentation and small-scale drug substance process capabilities—a truly one-of-a-kind asset within AZ Bio Ops. As Director of Biochemical & Biophysical Methods, you will lead a substantial part of this operation, managing a high-performing team of scientists who serve as subject matter experts (SMEs) for the biochemical and biophysical methods used to release and characterize our late-stage and commercial products. The team's core responsibilities include method validation and transfer, method lifecycle management, manufacturing investigation support, critical reagent qualification, and analytical testing in support of process improvement projects. You will also play a key strategic role in transforming analytical testing within AZ Bio by implementing innovative technologies, leveraging automation to replace manual workflows, and integrating advanced analytical technologies into upstream and downstream manufacturing processes. This is a leadership role where you will partner with peers across internal and external QC testing sites, other GTO functions, R&D, Quality, Regulatory, and Supply Chain organizations to ensure a continuous supply of medicines to patients.

**Typical Accountabilities:**
-----------------------------

* Lead a team that is responsible for execution of all biochemical and biophysical methods including capillary electrophoresis/focusing, HPLC, UPLC, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, differential scanning calorimetry, and various spectroscopic techniques. Execution of this suite of assays typically support method validation, analytical tech transfer, critical reagent qualification, and process improvement projects.

* Plays a key role in identifying and implementing improvement projects within the lab function including integration of automation/liquid handling into workflows, use of generative AI for report generation, data compilation, and review. Works cross-functionally with peers across the organization to help define next generation analytical strategy across the company.

* Maintain GTO’s lab space in a state of GMP compliance.

* Be able to troubleshoot biochemical and biophysical methods.

* **To succeed in this role, you will need to be self-motivated, innovative, have strong technical and communication skills, and a deep understanding of protein chemistry and relevant methods used to release biological products.**

* **Mentors and develops staff of approximately eight direct reports; this is a people manager role.**

**Education, Qualifications, Skills, and Experience**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree technical field such as Pharmacy, Biology, Chemistry.

* Preferred advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a scientific field

* Subject matter expert in multiple biochemical and biophysical methods including HPLC, UPLC, capillary electrophoresis/focusing, mass spectrometry, circular dichroism, and differential scanning calorimetry.

* Minimum 10 years of experience working in the pharmaceutical industry.

* Working experience in supervisory / managerial roles within quality in the Pharmaceutical Industry.

* Experience working with regulatory / SOP / GxP requirements and driving compliance.

* Leading complex projects / operations in terms of resources, vendors, and budgets.

* Driving substantial change initiatives through internal/external teams and partners

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $174,856-$262,285 USD However, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition, our positions offer a short-term incentive bonus opportunity; eligibility to participate in our equity-based long-term incentive program. Benefits offered included a qualified retirement program [401(k) plan]; paid vacation and holidays; paid leaves; and, health benefits including medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans. Additional details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment. If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That is why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that does not mean we are not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility.

**Date Posted**

16-Nov-2026

**Closing Date**

25-Feb-2027

Our mission is to build an inclusive environment where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and employees. In furtherance of that mission, we welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their protected characteristics. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please complete the corresponding section in the application form.

card.title: Chemical Manufacturing Plant Manager
card.description:
**Company Summary:**

We are a fast-growing, innovative company that is revolutionizing global health. At Vireo and pH-D you will be on the ground-floor of an exciting fast-growing company that focuses on its core values and is passionate about improving the lives of people and pets by delivering premium, health products through world-class research innovation and manufacturing.

**Position Summary:**

The Plant Manager has full operational accountability for the chemical manufacturing facility at Vireo Resources in Plattsmouth, Nebraska. This leader owns facility performance from raw material readiness through batch execution, finished product handoff, and shipment readiness. The role delivers safe, consistent, efficient, and cost-effective batches that meet approved specifications and production commitments, with direct accountability for people, production, manufacturing cost, equipment reliability, and continuous improvement.

**Role and Responsibilities:**

* **Operational Leadership:** Lead facility operations across all shifts, aligning production schedules, staffing, materials, and equipment availability to meet demand. Manage budgets and drive improvements in productivity, cost, quality, and delivery.
* **Process and Technical Leadership:** Apply chemistry and engineering expertise to improve manufacturing processes and resolve recurring issues. Partner with cross-functional teams to lead startups, establish operating standards, and ensure consistent execution of approved procedures.
* **Safety, Quality, and Compliance:** Ensure operations meet safety, environmental, and quality requirements. Oversee chemical handling, process safety, and emergency readiness, and lead corrective actions with EHS and Quality while preserving Quality’s independent product release authority.
* **People Leadership:** Hire, coach, and develop facility teams, ensuring effective shift coverage and employee competency. Establish clear expectations and reinforce accountability, collaboration, and Vireo’s core values.
* **Strategic Planning and Performance:** Develop capacity and improvement plans that support company growth. Execute approved capital projects and communicate operational results, financial performance, risks, and recovery plans to leadership.

**Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree or above in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related field.
* 8+ years in chemical manufacturing, including 3+ years leading plant operations. Experience must include people, production, and budget accountability.
* Proven batch manufacturing leadership with measurable improvements in yield, cycle time, quality, output, and cost.
* Strong budgeting, cost analysis, capacity planning, and KPI management skills.
* Strong knowledge of chemical processes, reaction engineering, utilities, and automated controls. Translate technical issues into practical decisions and communicate clearly.
* Ability to lead a 24/7 operation and respond to urgent operating issues.
* Proven ability to develop teams, set expectations, and hold employees accountable.
* Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis skills. Demonstrated success preventing recurring failures.
* Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, or similar improvement methods. Certification preferred.
* Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, quality, and compliance. Plant startup, commissioning, or expansion experience preferred.
* Travel up to 10%

**Physical Demands / Work Environment:**

* Ability to stand, walk, climb stairs, and perform essential plant duties, with or without reasonable accommodation up to 10 hours.
* Must be able to occasionally lift up to 50 pounds
* Ability to work around chemicals, heat, noise, and equipment using required safeguards and PPE.
* Availability for extended hours or weekends during startup, outages, emergencies, and critical operations.

**Compensation + Benefits:**

* Base salary + bonus based on company and personal performance
* Medical, Dental, Vision and Supplement Insurance (with company assistance)
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid Time off, 9.5 Paid Holidays

card.title: Sand Plant Manager
card.description:
**Job Description:** 
Responsible for the management of all aspects of a sand mining and production facility. This position will utilize budgets, production goals, and effective communication. Safety must be a top priority. 
 
**Job Requirements:** 
**ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 
 
Direct the following department personnel to ensure safety and productivity is achieved. 
1. Mine Team 
2. Wash Operators 
3. Dry Plant Operators 
4. Quality/Lab 
5. Maintenance

* Efficiently schedule and supervise hourly personnel for weekly operations, monitor timecards, vacations, and control overtime.
* Work with corporate HR department on staffing needs and employee issues.
* Handle discipline and grievances, as required, while maintaining acceptable labor and employee relations.
* Accurately collect, review, and forward operating data, such as mine, wash, and dry plant production reports.
* Assist HSE Coordinator in collecting the necessary data for MSHA and DNR reports.
* Communicate effectively and timely with owners, corporate directors, and/or other management of problems or potential problems that affect the proper operation of the plant. Problems may include personnel, equipment, transportation, quality, or raw materials.
* Direct activities safely to achieve optimum rates of productivity consistent with long/short range goals
* Direct and coordinate plant/mine related projects with Director of Mining
* Assisting in the preparation of capital projects and plan, and their completion • Direct and oversee activities performed by subcontractors.
* Monitor the mine operation to ensure compliance with all regulations concerning air emissions, water discharge, erosion and sedimentation control.
* Assist, implement, and comply with ISO 9001 quality program.
* Review quality reports daily and ensure quality standards are being followed.
* Evaluate with the EHS Coordinator the company’s training program and conditions in the plant, creating a culture of safety that exceeds MSHA guidelines and regulations.
* Ensure safety and good housekeeping by being active in all programs.
* Recommend and/or purchase materials and supplies as necessary, utilizing corporate purchasing department. Recommend equipment and process modifications to improve efficiencies.
* Ensure work standards, policies, plans, and procedures are enforced. Support management’s policies and programs.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIRMENTS**

* Team-oriented, an effective communicator (verbal and written), able to offer technical expertise and guidance, and have the ability and willingness to build rapport with department team members and external departments.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks and set priorities appropriately.
* Understanding our company functions as a cohesive operation, and often employees serve in many roles and various functions or capacities.
* Develop working relationships with other corporate personnel and plants.
* Maintain open communications with subordinates, peers, and superiors.
* Basic knowledge of Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s Degree, in Business Management or related field
* 3 to 5 years of related experience in a position of leadership, Surface Mining Experience preferred
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Advanced experience working with MSHA Safety and Environmental competency
* Supervisory skills
* Budgetary skills - Capital planning and projects
* Short and long-term planning and scheduling
* Leadership Skills

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Pass toxicity test.
* Medical clearance to wear respiratory protection.
* Team?oriented, effective communicator (verbal and written), able to offer technical expertise and guidance, and
* have the ability and willingness to build rapport with team members and external agencies.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks and set priorities appropriately.
* Willingness to further training or education, if requested.

card.title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)
card.description:
**Description**

 
 
 
 

Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) 
Department: EHSQ / Quality 
Location: Houston, TX

Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality 
Direct Reports: None 
FLSA Status: Exempt 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time

Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote

Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)

Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.

The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.

SUMMARY

The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on BESS scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers both standalone BESS facilities and BESS integrated with utility-scale solar PV projects.

The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active BESS construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of BESS Quality across the portfolio.

Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of utility-scale BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, power conversion systems (PCS) and inverters, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary power, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection, suppression, gas detection, and explosion control installation interfaces. Equally important is a working command of manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements, which often govern acceptance more directly than the project drawings. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, battery management and energy management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing remain with Engineering, Commissioning, and the manufacturer; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.

This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on standalone and PV-integrated BESS construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for BESS scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain BESS inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.

* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, manufacturer requirements, documentation requirements, and common BESS failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the BESS Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for BESS scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering and the manufacturer.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring BESS nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.

* Working knowledge of NFPA 855, NEC (NFPA 70) Article 706, UL 9540 and UL 9540A, and the energy storage provisions of the International Fire Code.
* Experience supporting BESS mechanical completion, construction completion, or commissioning-readiness documentation.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV, medium-voltage collection, or substation scopes adjacent to BESS installations.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, manufacturers, and external stakeholders.

card.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

Range of pay $34,216.00 - $62,100.00 Salary

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

* Breathe easy with **medical, dental, and vision** benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
* Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with **employee assistance programs.**
* Feel great and thrive with access to **health and wellness programs, paid time off** and **discounts** for work necessities, such as cell phones.
* … and much more.

 
In addition to the above pay rate, in the state of Minnesota we currently provide a $3.00 per hour premium on all classroom hours worked which is funded through the Minnesota Great Start Compensation Support Program.

We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

*KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.*

card.description:
***POSITION PURPOSE:***

The Director of Quality Improvement operates under the leadership and direction of the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Operating Officer (COO). The CMO maintains direct clinical oversight of clinical quality improvement activities and regulatory quality programs. The Director of Quality Improvement provides organization-wide leadership for EVCHC's quality improvement program. The Director establishes the quality strategy in partnership with executive, clinical, operational and compliance leaders; converts organizational goals and regulatory requirements into measurable work plans; and leads improvement efforts that strengthen patient outcomes, safety, access, equity and care experience. The Director is accountable for reliable quality data, required clinical quality reporting, continuous improvement methods, Patient Centered Medical Home recognition, and the performance of the Quality Improvement Department.

 

***MAJOR POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES AND FUNCTIONS:***

**Quality Strategy and Governance**

* Lead the development, implementation and annual evaluation of EVCHC's organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance Plan in alignment with the strategic plan, clinical standards and applicable Health Center Program requirements.

* Establish annual quality priorities, measures, targets, owners and timelines with executive and clinical leadership. Monitor progress and recommend corrective action when performance does not meet established goals.

* Lead or support the Quality Improvement Committee and related workgroups. Prepare agendas, dashboards, meeting materials, decisions and follow-up reports for executive leadership and the Board of Directors, as requested.

* Advise executive leaders on emerging quality risks, performance trends, resource needs and opportunities to improve care delivery across sites and service lines.

* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, patient safety and learning throughout the organization.

**Department Leadership**

* Direct the work of the Quality Improvement Department, including recruitment, onboarding, supervision, coaching, performance evaluation, workload assignment and staff development.

* Develop departmental goals, staffing plans, procedures and budgets that support timely completion of quality priorities and reporting obligations.

* Set clear expectations for the accuracy, timeliness and usability of analyses, audits, reports and improvement support provided by the department.

* Build effective working relationships with clinical care teams, Operations, Information Technology, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Behavioral Health, Dental and other departments involved in quality outcomes.

**Quality Measurement and Reporting**

* Oversee the collection, validation, analysis and submission of clinical quality measures and required reports, including Uniform Data System measures, population health platforms transition and readiness, HEDIS and payer measures, grant measures and internal quality indicators.

* Develop and maintain executive, provider, site and service-line dashboards that show current performance, trends, disparities, targets and improvement actions.

* Track provider and care-team performance, identify variation and care gaps, and provide leaders with actionable information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data-use standards.

* Establish data-validation controls and documentation so that quality reports can be reconciled to source systems and used as an organization-wide source of truth. Partnering with Director of Data and IT operations for oversight on data governance committee.

* Present quality findings in clear written and verbal reports to the Board, executive leadership, managers, providers, staff, health plans and external reviewers, as appropriate.

**Performance Improvement**

* Lead Plan Do Study Act cycles, root-cause analyses and other structured improvement methods from problem definition through implementation, evaluation and sustainment.

* Partner with clinical and operational leaders to improve preventive care, chronic disease outcomes, access, continuity, patient experience, care coordination, documentation and other priority measures.

* Translate data findings into practical workflow changes, training, decision support, audit tools and accountability processes that can be sustained across sites.

* Evaluate improvement results, identify lessons learned and spread effective practices to other care teams, programs or locations when appropriate **Regulatory Readiness and Patient Safety**

* Lead the quality components of Patient Centered Medical Home recognition and renewal, including evidence collection, workflow assessment, documentation, staff education and sustainment of recognized practices alongside Director of compliance.

* Partner with Compliance Director, Risk Management, clinical leadership and Operations on quality-related readiness for HRSA operational site visits, FTCA deeming and risk-management activities, health plan audits, accreditation reviews and other external assessments.

* Support corrective action plans with the Director of Compliance arising from audits, quality reviews, safety events or regulatory findings. Define measures, monitor completion and verify that corrective actions are effective and sustained.

* Analyze trends in patient safety events, grievances and quality-of-care concerns with the appropriate leaders while protecting confidentiality and following reporting requirements.

* Maintain organized records of quality plans, committee actions, reports, audits, improvement projects and supporting evidence required for oversight and external review.

**Clinical Analytics and Health Information Technology**

* Direct the clinical analytics program and define reporting requirements that support clinical decision-making, population health management and performance improvement.

* Partner with Information Technology and system vendors to improve data extraction, interfaces, registries, care guidelines, clinical decision support, templates and reporting tools used for quality measurement.

* Lead data-governance practices for quality information, including measure definitions, ownership, validation, access, change control and resolution of reporting discrepancies.

* Assess the quality and workflow impact of new digital tools and automation used in clinical or quality processes and recommend safeguards, testing and performance monitoring before broad implementation.

* Recommend redesign of workflows affected by the electronic health record, patient portal, population health platforms and other clinical information systems.

card.title: Senior Manager, Supplier Quality (R6220)
card.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **Job Description:**

Shield AI is actively seeking candidates with deep expertise in manufacturing and quality methodologies, paired with a relentless drive to enable supplier success and strengthen mission-critical operations.

Shield AI’s Supply Chain Quality team is responsible for global quality oversight across our supplier base. The team reduces supply-chain risk through supplier assessments and internal risk reviews, proactively drives supplier qualification and development activities.

In this role, you will lead a supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, development, performance management, and quality assurance across Shield AI’s aerospace and defense supply base. You will set supplier-quality priorities; manage team capacity, technical execution, and resource allocation; and develop high-performing quality leaders. The role also oversees supplier audits, nonconformance resolution, root-cause investigations, and hands on hardware dispositions.

You will evaluate supplier capability, quality performance, organizational risk, and resource needs to ensure purchased hardware and materials meet Shield AI engineering, customer, regulatory, and quality requirements. As an experienced aerospace quality leader, you will partner closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Program teams to resolve complex supplier-quality issues, improve supplier capability, and reduce quality and delivery risk across the supply base.

**What you'll do:**

* Develop the supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, surveillance, performance management, and corrective-action activities across Shield AI’s global aerospace and defense supply base.
* Establish supplier-quality priorities, allocate resources, and translate functional objectives into staffing, workload, and execution plans that support product, program, and organizational needs.
* Develop Supplier Quality leaders and engineering personnel through coaching, performance management, succession planning, workforce development, and technical mentorship.
* Oversee supplier qualification, risk assessments, periodic performance reviews, supplier audits, source inspections, and approved-supplier status across complex aerospace hardware, commodities, and manufacturing processes.
* Ensure supplier requirements are effectively flowed down and that suppliers comply with applicable quality management system, engineering, customer, contractual, regulatory, and statutory requirements.
* Escalate significant supplier-quality risks and direct SCARs, supplier recovery efforts, and capability-improvement plans that could affect product quality, delivery, mission readiness, or program execution.
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program teams to address supplier producibility, design-for-manufacturability, process capability, technical execution, and quality risks.
* Advance supplier-quality processes, business systems, data analytics, and continuous-improvement practices that strengthen supplier capability, product quality, delivery performance, and supply-base resilience.

**Required qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or another related technical discipline.
* At least 7 years of relevant experience, including 2–5 years of leadership or people-management experience with direct responsibility for Quality Engineering and/or Supplier Quality Engineering personnel.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and/or ISO 9001 quality-management systems, as well as aerospace and defense supplier-quality requirements.
* Demonstrated proficiency in root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methods, including 8D, 5 Whys, and fishbone analysis.
* Experience with supplier qualification, supplier development, PPAP, and First Article Inspection processes, including AS9102 requirements.
* Understanding of ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and other requirements applicable to aerospace and defense suppliers.
* Demonstrated people-leadership capability, including coaching, performance management, organizational development, and building high-performing technical teams.
* Strong cross-functional collaboration, executive communication, and supplier relationship-management skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.
* Experience using ERP/MRP systems.
* Ability to travel to Shield AI manufacturing locations and supplier sites domestically and, as needed, internationally—up to approximately 20% of the time.

**Preferred qualifications:**

* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), or equivalent quality certification.
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Experience leading supplier-quality functions in a high-growth aerospace, defense, autonomy, robotics, or advanced-manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting the production and qualification of complex electromechanical, electronic, precision-machined, composite, or avionics hardware.

card.title: Director, Quality Control (QC) GMP Analytical
card.description:
Franklin Biolabs emerges from the esteemed legacy of Dr. Jim Wilson's laboratory, a beacon of innovation in vector technology for over three decades. Building on this rich heritage, Franklin Biolabs is poised to redefine the landscape of the global genetic medicines industry. As a Contract Research Organization (CRO), Franklin Biolabs offers a comprehensive suite of services spanning from discovery through clinical manufacturing. Our goal is to empower our partners by providing unparalleled solutions that drive the advancement of genetic medicines. Leveraging decades of expertise and a commitment to excellence, we bridge the gap between groundbreaking research and ensuring that transformative therapies reach those who need them most.

Franklin Biolabs is in search of a successful QC GMP Analytical Laboratory Director who combines deep scientific expertise with proven regulatory knowledge and business leadership. The individual is capable of managing complex GMP testing operations, leading regulatory inspections, driving continuous improvement initiatives, developing high-performing teams, and ensuring the delivery of accurate, reliable, and compliant analytical results that support product quality and patient safety.

The Director of QC GMP Analytical Laboratory is responsible for the strategic leadership, operational management, and regulatory compliance of the Quality Control analytical testing laboratory supporting GMP manufacturing, product release, stability programs, method qualification/validation, and investigational/commercial products. This role ensures the generation of high-quality analytical data in compliance with FDA, EMA, ICH, USP, and applicable global regulatory requirements while maintaining inspection readiness and fostering a culture of quality, scientific excellence, and continuous improvement.

The Director provides leadership for laboratory personnel, oversees testing activities across multiple analytical platforms, manages laboratory budgets and resources, and serves as a key quality and technical representative during client interactions, regulatory inspections, and internal audits.

**Key Responsibilities**

Leadership & Laboratory Management

* Direct all QC analytical laboratory operations supporting GMP testing and product release.
* Develop and implement laboratory strategies aligned with organizational goals and regulatory requirements.
* Lead, mentor, and develop managers, scientists, analysts, and technical staff.
* Establish performance metrics and monitor laboratory productivity, turnaround times, and quality indicators.
* Build a culture focused on data integrity, compliance, quality, accountability, and scientific excellence.
* Manage staffing plans, succession planning, recruitment, and employee development.

GMP Compliance & Quality Systems

* Ensure laboratory activities comply with current GMP (cGMP), GLP where applicable, and data integrity requirements.
* Maintain inspection readiness for regulatory agencies and client audits.
* Lead investigations involving OOS, OOT, laboratory deviations, CAPAs, and change controls.
* Review and approve analytical reports, protocols, investigations, and technical documents.
* Ensure compliance with ALCOA+ principles for data integrity.
* Support responses to regulatory observations and inspection findings.

Analytical Testing Oversight

* Provide scientific and technical oversight for:
 + Chromatography (HPLC, UPLC, LC-MS/MS, GC)
 + Molecular assays (qPCR, ddPCR, NGS)
 + Cell-based assays and potency testing
 + Immunological assays (ELISA, MSD, flow cytometry)
 + Biophysical characterization methods
 - * Protein and peptide characterization
 * Stability studies
 * Environmental monitoring and raw material testing (as applicable)
 - Review analytical trends and implement corrective actions when necessary.
 - Oversee transfer, qualification, and validation of analytical methods.
 - Ensure timely completion of release and stability testing.
 + Regulatory & Inspection Support

 - Act as laboratory representative during:
 * FDA inspections
 * EMA inspections
 * Client audits
 * Internal quality audits
 * Accreditation assessments
 - Ensure laboratory documentation meets regulatory expectations.
 - Maintain awareness of evolving regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
 + Method Validation & Technical Excellence

 - Oversee method development, qualification, transfer, and validation activities.
 - Review protocols and reports for compliance with ICH and regulatory guidance.
 - Drive implementation of new technologies and analytical platforms.
 - Support technical troubleshooting and complex root cause investigations.
 + Operational Excellence

 - Develop and manage laboratory budgets and capital expenditures.
 - Ensure appropriate maintenance, qualification, and calibration of laboratory equipment.
 - Drive continuous improvement initiatives to improve efficiency, compliance, and quality.
 - Monitor laboratory KPIs, including:
 * Right-first-time performance
 * Deviation rates
 * CAPA effectiveness
 * Turnaround times
 * Instrument utilization
 * Training compliance
 + Client & Cross-Functional Support

 - Serve as a primary technical contact for clients and stakeholders.
 - Collaborate with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Process Development, and Project Management teams.
 - Support proposal development, technical assessments, and business development opportunities.
 - Present laboratory performance metrics and technical data to senior leadership and clients.

**Education and Experience**

* Ph.D. in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or related scientific discipline preferred.
* Master's degree with significant industry experience may be considered.
* Bachelor's degree with extensive leadership experience in GMP analytical laboratories may be considered.
* 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in GMP analytical testing.
* 5+ years in laboratory leadership or management roles.
* Experience supporting biologics, cell and gene therapy, vaccines, nucleic acid therapeutics, or pharmaceutical products.
* Demonstrated experience managing regulatory inspections and client audits.
* Experience leading method validation, qualification, and laboratory investigations.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Strong understanding of:
 + GMP regulations
 + FDA and EMA expectations
 + ICH guidelines
 + USP requirements
 + Data integrity regulations
 + Analytical method lifecycle management
* Expertise with one or more of the following:
 + LC-MS/MS
 + HPLC/UPLC
 + qPCR/ddPCR
 + Flow Cytometry
 + ELISA/MSD
 + Cell-based potency assays
 + Protein analytical characterization

Leadership Competencies

* Strategic thinking
* People development
* Regulatory decision-making
* Risk management
* Scientific problem solving
* Cross-functional collaboration
* Client relationship management
* Operational excellence
* Change leadership
* Continuous improvement mindset

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

* GMP compliance and inspection readiness
* On-time product release testing
* Investigation closure timelines
* CAPA effectiveness
* Laboratory utilization and efficiency
* Staff engagement and retention
* Client satisfaction
* Budget performance
* Method validation success rate
* Data integrity compliance metrics

**Essential Status**

* Not Applicable: The employee is not required to go on-site to perform their job functions during company closure.

**Vision**

* Ability to distinguish between different colors (normal color vision).
* Ability to see clearly at various distances.
* Adequate near vision for reading documents or lab equipment.
* Ability to focus and maintain concentration in tasks for extended periods.
* Ability to work in environments with varying light conditions.

**Company Benefits**

* 401(k)
* 401(k) Matching
* Health insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Health Savings Account and Flexible Spending Account
* Paid Time-Off
* Company Paid Holidays
* Personal Floating Holidays
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
* Life and AD&D insurance (Group & Voluntary)

card.description:
Overview:

The Director of Operations is responsible for overseeing and coordinating operations across all markets to ensure projects are properly planned, staffed, resourced, and executed safely, efficiently, and profitably. This position provides leadership and support to regional operations, field supervision, project management, and estimating while maintaining a strong focus on customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and company growth.

Responsibilities:

* **Scheduling & Resource Allocation:** Oversee companywide project scheduling, prioritize work, and allocate crews, equipment, and resources across all markets to maximize efficiency and utilization.
* **Crew Staffing & Workforce Planning:** Coordinate staffing needs, crew assignments, and workforce development to ensure adequate personnel are available to meet project demands.
* **Project Management & Estimating:** Provide oversight and direction to project management and estimating teams, ensuring accurate project handoffs, effective execution, cost control, and profitability.
* **Regional & Field Support:** Support regional managers and field supervisors with operational decisions, project execution, personnel management, and day-to-day challenges.
* **Material Forecasting & Planning:** Coordinate material forecasts, procurement planning, and delivery schedules to ensure timely availability of stabilization materials while minimizing downtime and costs.
* **Jobsite Troubleshooting:** Provide hands-on support in resolving field challenges involving soil conditions, equipment, production, scheduling, and constructability.
* **Engineering & Value Engineering:** Collaborate with engineers, customers, and project teams to identify value engineering (VE) opportunities and cost-effective stabilization solutions.
* **Preconstruction Planning:** Lead coordination between estimating, project management, and field operations to ensure project scope, schedules, manpower, equipment, materials, and potential risks are addressed before mobilization.
* **Customer Relationships:** Maintain a customer-focused approach, support key customer relationships, resolve project concerns, and ensure commitments are met.
* **Operational & Financial Performance:** Monitor project profitability, productivity, equipment utilization, scheduling performance, and operational costs while driving continuous improvement.
* **Safety & Quality:** Promote consistent safety standards, quality workmanship, accountability, and best operational practices across all markets.

Qualifications:

* **Qualifications**

 + 10+ years of experience in soil stabilization, heavy civil construction, earthwork, or related specialty contracting.
 + Proven experience managing multiple projects, crews, and geographic markets.
 + Strong understanding of construction operations, scheduling, equipment utilization, project management, and estimating.
 + Knowledge of soil stabilization methods, materials, equipment, and field applications preferred.
 + Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
 + Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on field support and operational decision-making.
 + Willingness to travel between markets and project locations as needed.

 **Key Performance Expectations**

 + Maximize crew and equipment utilization across all markets.
 + Maintain effective scheduling and project readiness.
 + Improve project productivity and profitability.
 + Minimize operational downtime and resource conflicts.
 + Strengthen regional and field leadership performance.
 + Deliver consistent quality and customer satisfaction.
 + Support sustainable company growth through efficient operations.

We seek the best solutions possible by attracting and engaging a diverse workforce where all perspectives are sought out and valued.

card.title: Market Director, Facility Operations
card.description:
**Join a team that shares your calling**

At MultiCare, you’re more than just a job title — you’re part of a team built on trust that cares for each other, our patients and our communities. Belonging here means living our mission and values every day. If your purpose and passions align with ours, you’ll find a place to grow, do meaningful work and build a career you love in a community that feels like home.

**FTE:** 1.0, **Shift:** Day, **Schedule:** Business hours

**Position Summary**

The Market Director, Facility Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for facility operations across the East Pierce Market within MultiCare Health System, including hospitals, ambulatory sites, urgent care centers, clinics, medical office buildings, and other healthcare facilities. 
 
This role is accountable for market-level facility operations, plant operations, building systems, property management, regulatory compliance, infrastructure reliability, and facility-related operational planning.
 
 
The Market Director serves as the primary operational partner between East Pierce Market leadership and system Facilities Management & Operations Support Services (FMOSS), Planning, Design & Construction, Real Estate, and other enterprise support teams. 
 
The position supports the growth and development of acute care, ambulatory, and ambulatory surgery center (ASC) services throughout the market by ensuring facility readiness, property management, operational integration, infrastructure performance, and strategic alignment with organizational objectives.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute market-based facility operations strategies that support MultiCare Health System goals, market growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and exceptional patient and caregiver experiences.
* Provide operational leadership for facility operations across East Pierce Market hospitals, ambulatory care centers, urgent care locations, clinics, medical office buildings, and future expansion sites.
* Administer and maintain departmental services in accordance with standards established by The Joint Commission, CMS, Washington State Department of Health, NFPA, OSHA, and other applicable regulatory agencies to ensure compliance and operational readiness.
* Oversee the operation, maintenance, reliability, and performance of facility infrastructure systems including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, medical gas, utility distribution, fire and life safety systems, and vertical transportation.
* Partner with system Planning, Design, Construction, Real Estate, FMOSS, and executive leadership teams to support enterprise capital initiatives, facility modernization programs, infrastructure investments, and market growth priorities.
* Provide local operational leadership and accountability for facility improvement projects, renovations, repairs, and capital projects within delegated market authority.
* Support the development and expansion of ambulatory care services and Ambulatory Surgery Centers (ASCs) through facility planning, operational readiness activities, site assessments, and coordination with system stakeholders.
* Contribute to long-range facility, infrastructure, and space planning efforts that support the East Pierce Market's strategic growth objectives.
* Oversee market property management activities, including leased and owned properties, landlord relationships, facility condition management, operational readiness, occupancy coordination, and vendor performance.
* Partner with Organizational Compliance, Environment of Care, Emergency Management, and Safety leaders to ensure effective implementation of Environment of Care, Life Safety, Emergency Preparedness, and related regulatory programs throughout the market.
* Manage resource allocation, operational budgets, workforce planning, contracted services, and performance metrics to optimize organizational effectiveness and asset stewardship.
* Facilitate coordination between hospital leadership, ambulatory leadership, physicians, FMOSS, and operational teams to ensure facility services support clinical and business objectives.
* Oversee minor construction, infrastructure upgrades, and facility enhancement projects while ensuring minimal disruption to patient care and business operations.
* Participate in market strategic planning initiatives and provide facility expertise to support operational growth, service line expansion, and future care delivery models.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, Business Administration, Engineering, Construction Management, Facilities Management, Public Administration, or related field required.
* Master's Degree preferred.
* Eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare facility operations, plant operations, property management, capital project coordination, regulatory compliance, engineering, or related operational leadership functions.
* Five (5) years of experience with The Joint Commission standards, including Environment of Care, Life Safety, Emergency Management, and regulatory compliance requirements.
* Five (5) years of management or supervisory experience with direct budget, operational, and personnel responsibilities.
* Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with planning, design, construction, real estate, property management, and executive leadership teams on healthcare facility initiatives.
* Experience supporting hospital and ambulatory healthcare operations in a multi-site healthcare environment preferred.
* Knowledge of healthcare facility infrastructure systems, regulatory requirements, facility operations, capital planning processes, and property management principles.

**About Good Samaritan Hospital**

MultiCare Good Samaritan Hospital is a 388-bed acute-care hub serving Puyallup and East Pierce County. As the area’s only hospital, it features a Family Birth Center, Level III Trauma and Neonatal ICUs, Level I Trauma Rehabilitation Center, Children’s Therapy Unit and a 24-hour Emergency Department. Innovative facilities like the LEED Gold-certified Dally Tower and Pulse Heart Institute make Good Samaritan a dynamic workplace for clinicians eager to advance their careers in a state-of-the-art environment.

**About the Puyallup Community**

Nestled at the foot of Mount Rainier along the Puyallup River, Puyallup offers a welcoming small-town feel just 10 miles from Tacoma and 35 miles from Seattle. Residents enjoy unique dining, an antique-filled downtown, excellent schools and abundant parks and recreation — all while being close to big-city opportunities.

**Why MultiCare?**

**Rooted in the local community**

Partnering with patients, families and neighbors across the Pacific Northwest for more than 140 years.

**Growth and education**

Competitive tuition assistance, award-winning residencies, fellowships and career development to invest in you.

**Well-being and support**

Generous PTO, Code Lavender and Employee Assistance Programs to help you maintain balance and feel cared in your work and life.

**Living our values**

Respect, integrity, kindness and collaboration guide how we care for patients, communities and each other.

**Belonging for all**

Resource Groups and outreach programs help ensure every team member feels safe, seen, heard and valued.

**Pacific Northwest lifestyle**

Work and live where natural beauty, adventure and strong community connections are part of everyday life.

**Pay and Benefit Expectations**

We provide a comprehensive benefits package, including competitive salary, medical, dental and retirement benefits and paid time off. As required by various pay transparency laws, we share a competitive range of compensation for candidates hired into each position. The pay scale is $163,113.60 - $234,707.20 USD. However, pay is influenced by factors specific to applicants, including but not limited to: skill set, level of experience, and certification(s) and/or education. If this position is associated with a union contract, pay will be reflective of the appropriate step on the pay scale to which the applicant’s years of experience align.

Associated benefit information can be viewed here.

The role will lead through influence across a matrixed organization, coordinating local, regional and national resources to achieve business objectives around producers and the point of sale, regardless of reporting structure. **Onco360 is continuing to grow, and we're seeking new team members. Join a mission-driven team making a difference in the lives of cancer patients.**

Our Onco360 Pharmacy has a need for a Director of Pharmacy Operations!

**Starting Pay:** **$160k and up, depending on experience** 
**Employment:** Full-Time

**Current Available Schedule:**

**Monday - Friday - 8am - 4:30pm EST**

**Onco360 Pharmacy is a unique oncology pharmacy model created to serve the needs of community, oncology and hematology physicians, patients, payers, and manufacturers.**

**We offer a variety of benefits** including: Medical; Dental; Vision; 401k opportunity; Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays; Tuition Reimbursement; Company paid benefits – life insurance; and short and long-term disability

A career with us is more than just a job. It's an opportunity to connect and care for our patients, providers, communities and each other. We attract extraordinary people who have a strong desire to live our mission - to better the lives of those battling cancer and rare diseases. Compassion is more important than numbers. We value teamwork, respect, integrity, and passion.

We succeed when you do, and our company and management team work hard to foster an environment that provides you with opportunities for both professional and personal growth.

***The Director of Pharmacy Operations will be responsible for the operation, direction, coordination, evaluation and management of the Pharmacy Operation. In addition, the Director of Pharmacy Operations will be responsible for the organization and implementation of policies and procedures that are established. The Director of Pharmacy Operations will participate in and oversee the pharmaceutical services to oncology patients in a manner that maximizes quality and patient safety.***

Director of Pharmacy Operations Major Responsibilities:

* Working in collaboration with Senior Director of Pharmacy Operations, the Director of Pharmacy Operations will determine the day-to-day priorities for the pharmacy staff and adjust those priorities as need be to meet the high touch needs of the pharmacy’s patients.
* The Director of Pharmacy Operations will ensure that prescription orders process through daily workflow in a timely manner
* Assists Senior Director in monitoring day-to-day pharmacy operations and driving workflow to ensure that the accurate and timely dispensing of quality pharmacy services is consistently delivered to all customers/residents using effective service leadership and customer skills.
* Develops creative solutions to workflow and process challenges and works with Senior Director and Operations Staff to implement changes or enhancements to process.
* Oversee workflow and coordinate with managers/supervisors/vertical leads on productivity and staff allocation to ensure timely prescription processing and accountability of performance
* Manages staff in a leadership role to maintain a positive working environment by creating synergy and teamwork to minimize employee relations issues and reduce turnover. Communicates effectively with coworkers and customers, and successfully resolves issues.
* Works with pharmacy management to control operating expenses by effective utilization of personnel, equipment and supplies to maintain and improve services within approved budget.
* Plan, organize and ensure adherence to Onco360 pharmacy policies and procedures.
* Interview, select and supervise the activities of the pharmacy staff; communicate interpret and discuss with staff policies and procedures.
* Determine job objectives, work methods and performance standards; review performance relative to departmental objectives; authorize and communicate salary changes, promotions, transfers, discipline and discharge and administer all other personnel actions when necessary to maintain consistent and productive workflow in the pharmacy.
* Appropriately recognize organizational lines within the department; keep employees informed of matters affecting their work and interest; interpret and explain policies and procedures, department objectives, operations, services, organization, budget and seek comments and suggestions form employees.
* Assure that professional competence of staff is maintained through education and coordination with senior staff. Plan for both short and long-range goals of the department in concert with the whole organizational plan of Onco360.
* Collaborates with healthcare team to provide clinical and technical support as needed.
* Delegate authority to pharmacy technicians to accomplish pharmacist supervised tasks. Provide authorization for supervision, orientation, training, job objectives, performance standards and appraisal, personal development, safety, communication, discipline, scheduling, grievances and other personnel actions.
* Provide for maintenance of appropriate records to assure that the quality, quantity and timeliness of work done is documented. Review and appraise work of others within the department; review and evaluate departmental performance; keep Senior Director informed of the department’s progress and problems and any significant factors affecting assigned responsibilities.
* Maintain competency in care for patients of all age groups and developmental stages, and maintain competency as specifically indicated by orientation guidelines for a unit.
* Conducts job responsibilities in accordance with the standards set out in the Company’s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, its policies and procedures, the Corporate Compliance Agreement, applicable federal and state laws, and applicable professional standards.
* The Director of Pharmacy Operations will adhere to all State and Federal laws and regulations with accepted standards of Onco360’s good pharmacy practices.
* Documentation of adverse events and products complaints per contractual obligations to pharmaceutical manufacturers.
* Other duties as required.

 

**Director of Pharmacy Operations Position Qualifications:**

Education/Learning Experience

* Required: High school diploma or equivalent. Combination of education, training, and relevant operational leadership experience sufficient to perform the responsibilities of the role.
* Desired: Bachelor’s degree (BSPh or Doctorate of Pharmacy (PharmD).

Work Experience

* Required: Required: 5+ years of progressive pharmacy experience, including experience leading teams, projects, or operational initiatives.
* Desired: 7+ years of progressive pharmacy experience. Specialty pharmacy experience.

Skills/Knowledge

* Required: Knowledge of pharmacy laws and federal and state regulations. Ability to work cooperatively as a member of a team. Extensive experience working in CPR+. Effective communication, problem-solving, and professional decision-making skills
* Desired: Previous leadership experience, competency with various Microsoft platforms (Excel, Word, Outlook), Ability to analyze performance data, identify trends, and implement improvements

Licenses/Certifications

* Required: Certified Pharmacy Technician license (CPhT) or RPH license in applicable state(s).
* Desired: Certified Pharmacy Technician (CPhT), Advanced Certified Pharmacy Technician (CPhT-Adv), Multi-State RPh licenses, Certified Specialty Pharmacist (CSP)

**Company Values: Teamwork, Respect, Integrity, Passion**

card.description:
Livingston Associates has partnered with an established company, made up of highly skilled, capable individuals who are looking to add a Director of Operations to their growing team! 
 
**Position Summary:** 
The Director of Operations is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations for a specialty contractor with multiple offices in NYS, ensuring projects are executed safely, efficiently, and profitably. This role partners closely with the CEO/Owner to translate strategic goals into executable plans across field operations, labor, scheduling, safety, compliance, and internal processes.. This position should be filled with a proven hands-on leader who can operate independently, make sound business decisions, manage multiple operational priorities, and contribute strategically to the company's overall success. 
 
**Compensation:**

* **$**130,000-$160,000 per year

 
**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Operations & Field Execution**:
 + Oversee daily operations across all projects, ensuring schedules, budgets, and quality standards are met
 + Coordinate closely with Field Operations, Safety & Compliance and project managers to support successful project delivery
 + Resolve operational issues impacting productivity, customer satisfaction, or safety
 + Ensure materials, labor, equipment are properly aligned with project needs
* **Financial & Performance Management**
 + Support job cost controls, labor efficiency, and margin performance
 + Monitor KPIs related to productivity, safety, schedule adherence, and profitability
 + Collaborate with accounting and project teams on forecasting, labor planning, and cash flow management
* **Labor & Workforce Management**
 + Partner with field operations for workforce planning, labor projections, and staffing levels
 + Support hiring, onboarding, training, and development of field and operations staff
 + Foster a culture of accountability, teamwork, and high performance
* **Safety, Compliance & Risk Management**
 + Partner with safety & compliance team to ensure compliance with OSHA, regulatory requirements, and company safety programs
 + Promote a strong safety-first culture across all field and office operations
 + Identify and mitigate operational and contractual risks
* **Process Improvement & Systems**
 + Develop, implement, and refine operational processes to improve efficiency and scalability
 + Lead adoption of tools, technology, and systems that streamline operations and reporting
 + Standardize best practices across projects and teams
* **Leadership & Strategy**
 + Partner with the CEO on strategic planning, growth initiatives, and operational alignment
 + Provide leadership, mentorship, and direction to operations team members
 + Support customer relationships and assist with issue resolution as needed

 
**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field preferred. Equivalent industry experience will be considered.
* Minimum of 10–15 years of progressive experience in commercial construction or specialty contracting.
* Minimum of 5–7 years in a senior operational leadership position with direct responsibility for project execution, personnel management, and financial performance.
* Demonstrated success managing operations for a construction company or division generating $20M–$40M+ in annual revenue.
* Experience overseeing multiple project teams and simultaneous projects across various geographic markets.

 
**Benefits & Incentives:**

* Paid time off
* Sick time
* 6 paid company holidays
* Health, Dental & Vision plan options
* Car allowance
* Fuel card
* 401(k) plan
* Professional development
* Short- & Long-term disability
* Life insurance
* Company/Team events
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Coordinated Services Management (CSM) is an established senior living management company serving nonprofit and mission-driven organizations throughout Virginia. We are seeking an experienced Regional Director of Operations to provide leadership, guidance, and operational oversight for assigned skilled nursing, assisted living and memory care communities in Virginia. This position is based in Roanoke and requires regular travel to assigned communities.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, results-oriented leader with strong operational and financial management skills, sound clinical knowledge, and a commitment to quality resident care and services.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership, coaching, and operational oversight to community Executive Directors and leadership teams.
* Drive operational excellence, regulatory compliance, quality of care, resident satisfaction, and financial performance.
* Monitor occupancy, marketing effectiveness, staffing, budgets, and financial results, identifying opportunities for improvement and growth.
* Partner with community leadership and home office team to address operational challenges and implement effective solutions.
* Support leadership development, performance management, and succession planning.
* Guide strategic planning, capital improvements, and effective stewardship of community resources.
* Collaborate with nonprofit ownership Boards, presenting operational results, financial performance, budgets, and strategic recommendations.
* Support the mission, values, and long-term success of each community and its nonprofit ownership.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, nursing, or a related field.
* Licensed Nursing Home Administrator with a minimum of three years of Executive Director experience.
* Strong understanding of senior living operations, regulatory compliance, and resident care practices; clinical experience is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated success in leadership development, financial management, and operational improvement.
* Excellent communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Multi-community leadership experience and experience with nonprofit organizations preferred.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
* Ability to travel throughout Virginia, including occasional overnight travel.

**Compensation**

Competitive salary commensurate with experience and qualifications.

**Join CSM and make a meaningful difference in the lives of seniors while supporting the success of mission-driven communities.**

Coordinated Services Management is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

card.description:
**The Director of Operations/Master Orchestrator** we want on our Pro Roofers Dream Team is someone who thrives on turning all the moving parts into a well-oiled machine! You are a natural leader who sees the big picture without ever losing sight of the details. Where others see obstacles, you see solutions. Where others see disorganization, you see an opportunity to build a better system.

You get a genuine sense of satisfaction from watching a team operate at its best because you've put the right people, processes, and expectations in place. You love numbers because they tell a story, and you know how to use that story to make things better. You're not afraid to roll up your sleeves, tackle a problem head-on, or have the tough conversations that keep everyone moving forward.

You're organized without being rigid and driven without losing your good nature. You know how to bring out the best in people while holding them accountable for results. You're a builder of systems, a solver of problems, and a master of follow-through. Most importantly, you take genuine pride in creating an operation that runs smoothly, profitably, and with excellence.

Job Duties/Responsibilities

* Be the driving force behind the day-to-day operations of Pro Roofers, ensuring everything runs efficiently from signed contract to completed project and final payment.
* Lead, support, and hold production teams accountable for completing jobs on time, within budget, and to our high standards of quality.
* Masterfully coordinate scheduling, material ordering, production, quality control, and billing to keep every job moving forward.
* Develop and maintain quality control processes that ensure exceptional workmanship and customer satisfaction.
* Keep a watchful eye on the production pipeline, anticipating problems and removing bottlenecks before they become costly.
* Track job costs, profit margins, and operational performance. You know your numbers and use them to make smart decisions!
* Create and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) that keep the team focused on measurable results.
* Keep our CRM accurate, organized, and functioning as a valuable management tool.
* Lead productive team meetings and individual check-ins that create clarity, accountability, and momentum.
* Build, document, and continually improve systems that make our operations more efficient and scalable.
* Embrace technology, software, and AI tools to simplify processes and help our team work smarter.
* Partner with our sales leadership to ensure a seamless transition from the sale to successful project completion.
* Cultivate a team environment built on trust, excellence, personal responsibility, and a shared commitment to success.

Qualifications

* Proven experience managing operations in the roofing or solar industry.
* A natural ability to lead people, build strong relationships, and inspire accountability.
* Exceptional organizational skills with an almost instinctive ability to identify what needs attention.
* A strong understanding of job costing, profit margins, budgets, and operational performance metrics.
* A numbers-driven mindset. You appreciate accurate data and know how to turn it into actionable improvements.
* Experience implementing and improving operational systems and procedures.
* Confidence working with CRM systems and business management software.
* An appreciation for emerging technology, including AI, and its ability to improve business efficiency.
* Strong communication skills and the ability to navigate challenging conversations with professionalism.
* A commitment to quality, consistency, and doing things right the first time.
* A proactive, solution-oriented attitude. You don't wait for someone else to fix a problem. You take ownership and get it done!
* Willingness to work long hours during the busy season.
* Agility to climb on a roof and walk the ridge.

Job Details

Position: Director of Operations

Location: Kansas City Area (On-site and in the field)

Job Type: Full-time

Compensation: 90, 000–130,000 annually, depending on experience

Competitive Compensation and Other Perks

A competitive salary that recognizes the value of your experience and leadership.

A positive, uplifting work environment focused on trust, service, excellence, teamwork, and growth.

A meaningful leadership position where your ideas, decisions, and contributions directly impact the company's success.

The opportunity to build and shape systems that support a growing and successful business.

The satisfaction of working alongside a motivated sales leader who values your operational expertise and trusts you to lead.

Professional growth opportunities as you help take Pro Roofers to the next level.

About Pro Roofers

The team at Pro Roofers brings over 20 years of residential and commercial roofing experience to the Kansas City area. We have built our reputation by delivering on our promises, doing quality work, and treating our customers and their homes with the care and respect they deserve. We have over 500 five star reviews and have earned every one of them by adhering to excellence.

At Pro Roofers, we believe that exceptional results come from exceptional people working together toward a common goal. We are guided by the principles of trust, growth, excellence, teamwork, and service.

We also understand the value of your home life and your work life, and we seek to enhance both. As part of the Pro Roofers Dream Team, your leadership will matter and your contributions will make a difference.

We're not just looking for someone to manage operations. We're looking for someone who will take ownership, build something exceptional, and take pride in the success of the entire team.

Ready to Work Your Magic? If you're the kind of leader who gets excited about building great systems, developing great people, and turning operational challenges into measurable success, we want to meet you!

To Apply: Send your resume along with a short note describing an operational process you built or improved, and the results it produced.

We can't wait to meet the next Master Orchestrator of our Pro Roofers Dream Team!

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $90,000.00 - $130,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Experience:

* Operations Coordination: 3 years (Preferred)
* Roofing: 1 year (Preferred)

Ability to Commute:

* Blue Springs, MO 64015 (Preferred)

Ability to Relocate:

* Blue Springs, MO 64015: Relocate before starting work (Preferred)

Work Location: In person
