card.description:
**Leading the Change in Youth Development**

At Boys & Girls Clubs of King County, we are taking youth programming to a new level. We are one of the largest Club organizations in the country, and we pride ourselves on always doing what is best for youth. As leaders in youth development, we provide a safe place for kids and teens during critical out-of-school time that is affordable for all families. Our Clubs offer life-changing programs and services to youth in greater Seattle. We prioritize a youth-centric Club experience through culturally relevant, inclusive, and diverse programming delivered by individuals committed to serving youth.

Our organization values advancing racial equity, creating safe spaces, encouraging collaboration and accountability, and seeking transparent and authentic communication. If you are passionate about youth development, love to connect with people, have a proven track record of results with youth, and want to be part of an extraordinary team, Boys & Girls Clubs of King County is right for you!!

**Opportunity Overview: CLUB OPERATIONS DIRECTOR**

Deliver excellence through leading a single or multiple Club responsibility ensuring the highest quality programs, services delivery and safe, healthy facilities for its members, employees, and the community. Recruit, coach and inspire employees to deliver a culturally relevant Club(s) Experience through diverse, inclusive programming. Achieve continuous improvement in program quality, facilities and operations and all expected metrics. Prepare, manage and achieve the Club(s) operating budget. Oversee the day-to-day management of the Club(s); its programs, employees and facilities. Participate with Club Advisory Boards and develop appropriate community engagement. Lead work with the Area Director, Club Service Center, and other Club Operations to maximize program capacities, Adelante Initiatives, to increase ADA and ensure that all safety policies are being followed.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Inspire and develop employees to live the mission, vision and values of the organization while delivering an outcome-driven club experience for youth and families. Encourage advancement of employees throughout the county to achieve larger roles and responsibilities and ability to increase compensation.
* Ensure all employees including the Operations Director, have continuous relevant trainings and expertise in all safety protocols/expectations, Race, Equity and Inclusion, exposure to all county and BGCA trainings, Affinity Groups and workshops. Inspire youth and employee voices continuously.
* Multiple Club responsibility to include one or more Licensed Childcare operations. Lead, coach and ensure all licensed program rules if applicable, protocols and expectations are being followed by directors and YDPs. Track STARS trainings/Merit Audits and annual renewals. Develop strong relationships with state and city licensors.
* Ensure that each Club provides the Support Protocol training and expectations; pertinent registration details to be updated in youth files, update of monthly meetings, providing extra support for parent meetings.
* Develop and advance strong relationships between school districts and other local community-based organizations.
* Ensure all registration processes and management of accounts are accurate and updated monthly. Lower A/Rs continuously and review results monthly with Area Director. Review and make sure that all county and BGCA measurement of metrics are consistently accurate.
* Achieve maximum capacity in all programs including elementary, teen, athletics. Lead Reach More Youth in area of responsibility. Always looking to serve more youth especially those that need us most. Lead RFP process for new Clubs.
* Achieve continuous improvement in all BGCA, state and local program measurements.
* Work with directors to achieve continuous improvement in quality of programs utilizing all relevant support.
* Provide continuous involvement in achieving financial health of each Club: efficient spending, achieve BVA goals, looking for better operational ways to achieve results.
* Ensure that physical Club is safe and healthy at all times and that appropriate maintenance is completed timely and efficient as well as large projects are communicated in a timely manner to Area Director. Create high standards for the common areas and outside of the Club. Work closely with vendors to make sure they are providing expected services in timely manner. Review all invoices for accuracy and timely payment.
* Work collaboratively with Chief Development Officer (CDO), Resource Development Team, and Area Director in fund development efforts. Support role in community centric fundraising. Work with Club Directors to develop Club Advisory Board and community partnerships.
* Report timely outcomes and utilize data to make changes that improve the outcome driven club experience.
* Enhance good public relations including speaking and presenting in public forums, building and sustaining partnerships with parents and families, stakeholders, community agencies and partners.
* Collaborate with council, committees, partner agencies and all stakeholders.
* Through effective delegation and oversight, assure effective administrative functions including data management, financial and bookkeeping files, personnel files, metric recording and reporting, and background checks.
* Maintain close, daily contact with Club staff (professional and volunteer), Club members to receive/provide information, discuss issues, explain or interpret guidelines/instructions; instruct, and advise/counsel, collaborate and partner on appropriate committees and task forces.
* Maintain close contact and work collaboratively with Area Directors, Area Director Program or Operations Leads and other Club Directors and peers.

**Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

* Bachelor’s Degree preferred in related field from an accredited college or university, and/or five (5) years applicable experience, preferably in Human Services, Non-Profit Management, or Public Administration.
* At least 2 years of direct management experience in a youth development setting with ability to successfully train and develop staff and volunteers.
* Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite.
* Ability to manage databases, collection information and pull accurate reports. (MyClubHub)
* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, professional presence, and strong customer service skills with the ability to maintain strict confidentiality.
* Ability to support fundraising efforts of the organization.
* Knowledge of budget preparation, control, and management.
* Ability to implement, train and support youth discipline techniques through organizational youth development philosophy.
* Satisfactory Motor Vehicle Record as determined by BGCKC Vehicle Loss Prevention Program, must be 18 years old or older and have at least 3 years of driving experience to drive Club owned and operated vehicles.

**Requirements for staff applying to Licensed Program Sites:**

Must have the qualifications explained below to support a Licensed Program or directly support the Club’s Program Director with the qualifications explained below:

**WAC** **110-305-1710** **Program director**. (1) The licensee must serve as or employ a program director who is responsible for the overall management of the child care program and operation. (2) The program director must have the understanding, ability, physical health, emotional stability and good judgment to meet the needs of the children in care. (3) The program director must: (a) Be at least twenty-one years of age; (b) Have two years' experience in management, supervision, or leadership; (c) Attend a department orientation within six months of employment or assuming the position; (d) Have a TB test as required under WAC 170-297-1750; (e) Have a background clearance as required under chapter 170-06 WAC; (f) Have current CPR and first-aid certification as required un[1]der WAC 170-297-1825; (g) Complete HIV/AIDS training and annual bloodborne pathogens training as required under WAC 170-297-1850; (h) Have a high school diploma or equivalent; (i) Have a minimum of forty-five college credits (or thirty college credits and one hundred fifty training hours) in approved school age credits as specified in the Washington state guidelines for deter- mining related degree and approved credits; and (j) Have completed basic STARS training or possess an exemption. (4) A program director must be on the premises as needed. (5) When the program director is not on-site the program director must leave a competent, designated staff person in charge. This staff person must meet the qualifications of a site coordinator and may also serve as child care staff when that role does not interfere with management and supervisory responsibilities. [WSR 18-14-078, re-codified as § 110-305-1710, filed 6/29/18, effective 7/1/18. Statutory Authority: RCW 43.215.060, 43.215.070, and chapter 43.215 RCW. WSR 15-01-046, § 170-297-1710, filed 12/9/14, effective 1/9/15. Statutory Authority: Chapter 43.215 RCW. WSR 12-23-057, § 170- 297-1710, filed 11/19/12, effective 12/20/12.

**HOURS:** Regular Full-Time, 40 Hours Per Week 
**FLSA:** Salaried, Exempt

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING ENVIRONMENT:**

*The physical demands and characteristics of the work environment described here are representative of those occurring in the performance of the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

While performing the essential functions of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

This position works in a club environment, and the noise level in the work environment can be loud to moderate. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to toxic or caustic chemicals, i.e. copier toner.

**DISCLAIMER:**

*This position description* *generally* *describes the principle functions of the position and the level of knowledge and skills typically required. It does not constitute an employment agreement between the employer and employee, and it is subject to change as the needs of the employer and the requirements of the job change.*

**Equal Employment Opportunity and Non-Discrimination**

Boys & Girls Clubs of King County (BGCKC) is committed to equal opportunity for all employees and applicants. BGCKC does not discriminate with regards to hiring, assignment, promotion or other conditions of staff employment because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, veteran status, disability, genetic information or any other status protected under local, state or federal law.

*In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, upon request, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of our positions.*
